question: Can the symmetries around a curve identify its rational points?
idea: The claim matches points on certain curves with compatible ways of splitting an arithmetic symmetry group. It covers all smooth proper curves of genus at least two over the stated p-adic fields, and specified modular curves over the rational numbers. It does not assert the rational-field case for every curve.
why: The study of whole numbers, primes, and equations. A simple question about numbers can hide an extremely difficult pattern.

glossary.meaning: A rational number is a number that can be written as a fraction of two integers.

exactClaim: Proves that rational points on every smooth proper geometrically connected curve of genus at least two over a finite extension of ℚp correspond bijectively to conjugacy classes of sections of its full arithmetic étale fundamental group. It also proves Grothendieck's section conjecture over ℚ for the modular curves $X_0(N)$ and $X_1(N)$ of genus at least two.
